core_obligations: Exhibit the two short exact sequences 0 -> I F -> F -> Q_1 -> 0 and 0 -> I F -> F tensor L -> Q_2 -> 0 from the regular-section construction, and bound the delta-dimension of the support of Q_1 and Q_2 by k (proof lines 18715-18721).
Record that the restrictions s_i of s to the components of delta-dimension k+1 are again regular meromorphic sections for the restricted invertible module (proof lines 18722-18724).

Reduce the cycle identity to a coefficient computation: for an integral closed subscheme Z of delta-dimension k with generic point xi, set A = O_{X, xi}, M = F_xi, choose a generator s_xi of L_xi, write s = (a/b) s_xi with a and b nonzerodivisors, and identify I_xi = {x in A | x(a/b) in A}, so that the coefficient of [Z] on the left is length_A(M/(a/b)IM) - length_A(M/IM) and on the right is the sum over the minimal primes q_i of the one dimensional local ring A of length_{A_{q_i}}(M_{q_i}) ord_{A/q_i}(a/b) (proof lines 18732-18751).
Conclude the two displayed identities in Z_k(X) and in CH_k(X) by invoking the module-level lemma for the coefficient comparison (proof lines 18725-18752).
proof_roadmap: Get the two sequences with the support bound for the quotient sheaves (proof lines 18715-18721).
Observe that the restrictions of the regular meromorphic section to the top dimensional components stay regular meromorphic (proof lines 18722-18724).
Reduce the cycle identity to a coefficient identity at the generic point of every k-dimensional integral closed subscheme and apply the module-level lemma (proof lines 18732-18752).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is stated for an invertible module L on a scheme X locally of finite type over a base situation, a coherent sheaf F with support all of X and no embedded associated points, X of delta-dimension at most k+1 with no embedded points, and a regular meromorphic section s; it asserts two short exact sequences starting in I F, that the cokernels Q_1, Q_2 have delta-dimension at most k, that s restricts to a regular meromorphic section on each component of dimension k+1, and that [Q_2]_k - [Q_1]_k equals both the explicit divisor sum and the cap product c_1(L) cap [F]_{k+1} in CH_k(X) (statement lines 18648-18712). The proof exhibits the two injections via the regular-section construction, gets the support bound from the nowhere dense support of the cokernels, and then reduces the cycle identity to a computation at the generic point xi of an arbitrary integral closed subscheme Z of delta-dimension k: writing s = (a/b) s_xi with a, b nonzerodivisors in A = O_{X, xi}, it identifies the coefficient of [Z] on the left as length_A(M/(a/b)IM) - length_A(M/IM) and on the right as the sum over the minimal primes q_i of A of length_{A_{q_i}}(M_{q_i}) ord_{A/q_i}(a/b), then quotes the module-level lemma (proof lines 18715-18752). Recognising the coefficient computation as an instance of the module statement is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
